- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for short-term (1–7d) to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated downward momentum; cap forecast decline to 15–25% of peak within 3–5d.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 10–30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 5–10% upward bias to forecast for 10–30d if sentiment is 0.33–0.67.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates true values when sentiment is negative or mixed; apply 10–15% upward adjustment if sentiment average < 0.50 over last 7d.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; add 2–5d buffer to forecast for 30d horizon to account for delayed reaction.
